prerequisites: Mathematics: Calculus II and Differential Equations

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the basic principles of fluid motion
Ability to calculate pipes and channels
Ability to know and master the tools used to address fluid flow problems
Ability to handle fluid magnitude meters

syllabus_topics: Concept of pressure. Pressure at a point
Various expressions of the continuity equation
Deformations and stresses in a real fluid
Extension of the case of external work applied to the control volume. Application to hydraulic machinery
DIMENSIONLESS GROUPS OF IMPORTANCE IN FLUID MECHANICS
HEAD LOSS IN TURBULENT FLOWS IN CONDUITS
FLUID FLOWS IN VARIABLE SECTION CONDUITS
Establishment of steady state in a pipe
VISCOSITY. NEWTONIAN FLUIDS. Exercises. Practical application: VISCOSIMETERS
GOVERNING EQUATIONS. Exercises. Pitot tube. Practical application: FREE JET. Radial velocity distribution. Turbulence in unconfined flows. Mass flow rate. Momentum

DIMENSIONAL ANALYSIS AND SIMILARITY. Exercises. Practical application: WIND TUNNEL. Pressure distribution around a cylinder. Drag coefficient calculation. Pressure distribution around an airfoil. Lift coefficient calculation.
FLOWS IN CONDUITS. REYNOLDS EXPERIMENT. Transition from laminar to turbulent regime.

HEAD LOSS AND FLOW METERS. Exercises. Practical applications: Flow measurement with venturimeter. Flow measurement with orifice plate. Friction coefficient. Head losses in elbows. Head losses in valves.
PIPE TRANSIENTS. Exercises. Practical application: WATER HAMMER. Pressure surges in a pipe. Operating mode of a surge tank.
assessment_rules: Students can choose between continuous or global assessment. For continuous assessment, the final grade is calculated as 0.4 times the first partial test (P1) + 0.4 times the second partial test (P2) + 0.2 times the continuous assessment of practical sessions (BP). Minimum requirements for continuous assessment are obtaining at least 4.0 out of 10 in P1, P2, and BP, and completing at least 80% of scheduled practical assessment tests. Global assessment consists of a single comprehensive test covering theoretical, practical, and problem-solving aspects, including practical content, with a maximum score of 100%. For both modes, a minimum of 4.0 out of 10 is required in each part of the test. For the second opportunity (resit), the global assessment method is the same, while for continuous assessment, three new partial recovery tests are offered, allowing students to keep previously obtained scores. To pass the course, a final grade equal to or greater than 5.0 out of 10 and fulfillment of all minimum requirements are necessary; otherwise, the maximum possible grade will be 4.9.
